pr_title: Implementations of new HttpContent sync methods.
pr_body:
Adds missing overrides of sync `SerializeToStream` and `CreateContentReadStream` to other `HttpContent` implementations in libraries.

Fixes #37477

cc: @Jozkee @GrabYourPitchforks @stephentoub @scalablecory

review_comments: Can we add tests that exercise these sync methods?
Nevermind; I see you did below.  Do those provide coverage for all of the added overrides?
Added extra test for `CopyTo` that hits sync `SerializeToStream`.
Unfortunately, this was not regenerated in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/37494

If the base SerializeToStream throws a NotSupportedException, does this mean we have a test hole?  Otherwise, I'd have expected the lack of an override here to result in NSEs in the HttpClient.Send PR.

We have a test hole, [Decompression tests ](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/Common/tests/System/Net/Http/HttpClientHandlerTest.Decompression.cs) aren't being run for sync scenario. I'm adding them.
It manifests if you have buffered, decompressed content.
Added decompression tests for sync scenarios.
I know this is still an `async` method but given that it is no longer used only by `SerializedToStreamAsync`, can we rename it to `SerializeToStreamCore`?
The param `async` already indicates if the method will use async APIs or not, what's the point of keeping the "Async" in the method name?

What is this accomplishing? Shouldn't the client's `DefaultRequestVersion` be the same as `remoteServer.HttpVersion` here? `HttpClient` does essentially the same thing as this `CreateRequest` when you call `GetAsync`.

`SendAsync|Send` ignores `HttpClient.DefaultRequestVersion` since it accepts fully constructed request. The default initialization of [`HttpRequestMessage`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d927afce85f66f80e82a7a74adf01ee3692caa1a/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/HttpRequestMessage.cs#L194) will set it to [1.1](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d927afce85f66f80e82a7a74adf01ee3692caa1a/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/HttpUtilities.cs#L12). And because we plug in [`VersionChecker`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d927afce85f66f80e82a7a74adf01ee3692caa1a/src/libraries/Common/tests/System/Net/Http/HttpClientHandlerTestBase.cs#L92) set up with the remote server version, it will blow up for 2.0 servers.

If it's about why `Send` versus `Get`, then it's because we weren't testing decompression with sync code paths at all due to using `GetAsync` (helpers didn't get sync overloads). And we had an error in missing overrides for decompression content :disappointed: So I changed the tests to use `SendAsync|Send` instead and now we're testing both, sync and async.
Just curious, what's the reason to add another property?
To test the camel-casing of property name when serialized through the workaround I did. All the existing have only 1 word name.
